7.  Pour this mixture into a 9" pie pan, and smooth it out with a spatula.

Sure, I can explain the basics. There are two types of GPS systems: 1) wireless, where a satellite in orbit passes overhead regularly and the receiver detects the signal and calculates its position, and 2) stationary, where the GPS receiver is placed somewhere in the landscape and tracks the signals as they travel.  GPS receivers use a technique called triangulation to estimate their own position. There are two key components to triangulation:

The most basic form of triangulation estimates your position by measuring other nearby signals, and calculates its own position based on the difference between those readings. This is why phones that are in proximity to one another are usually more accurate. For example, if it's the morning and you step out of bed, the satellite passageway is the only signal visible, your position should be accurate. In the evening, as many satellites are circling overhead, there will be many other signals available. 

The more sophisticated triangulation uses a measurement of the time it takes for a signal to travel from the receiver to the satellites to determine your position, and it relies on a measurement of the sidereal time.

Sfincione Recipe
------------
Sfincione di Mala Marina
2 lbs. (1 kg) tomatoes, roughly chopped 2 large onions, finely chopped 1/2 cup (125 grams) fennel, roughly chopped 2 garlic cloves, minced (or 1 T. unsalted butter) salt to taste about 1/4 c. ground black pepper 2 tbsp. unsalted butter
Cook fennel, garlic, and tomatoes in 2 T. olive oil in a 3-quart pot over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes are very soft, about 30 minutes. Uncover and let tomatoes steam for about 10 more minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Cut the tomatoes into chunks and add back in the pot with the onions and fennel. Mash with a potato masher.
Transfer tomato mixture to a large bowl and stir in butter and 1 tbsp. salt.
Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). 
Mix together all remaining ingredients (except butter) in another bowl. Add butter, mix lightly. 
Roll dough into balls about the size of a golf ball, place on a baking sheet. Bake for about 20-25 minutes, until lightly golden.
Remove from oven. 
Scoop tomato-butter mixture into each ball and roll into a ball. Cut each ball into eight pieces.
